gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus only the three leftmost NEMA 5-20R outlets give UPS backup. Anker's page marks the TT-30R 'No UPS', caps bypass at 1,440 W while the unit is charging from a 120 V wall outlet, and lists those same three UPS outlets as unusable when a generator feeds the unit. A sump pump left on standby therefore has to go in one of those three outlets, and you have to move it to the TT-30R or L14-30R when a generator is running the station.
standout_why: I checked RunTimeFit (cited), Tested Watts (cited) and OutageReadyHQ (cited). RunTimeFit says nothing about UPS, outlets or expansion batteries. Tested Watts says UPS stations 'switch in 10–20 ms' but names no outlet or bypass limits. OutageReadyHQ lists the F3800 Plus without a switchover time and says it expands, but not with which battery. No rival gives the outlet-by-outlet UPS map, the bypass wattage limits (F3800 Plus 1,440 W, Elite 300 1,800 W), or the fact that the Elite 300's 4,800 W 'lifting' figure covers only pure resistive loads.
decides: This confirms the setup more than it changes the pick. A 1/3 HP pump (about 800 W running in ChatGPT's own tables) fits under both bypass limits, so the F3800 Plus and Elite 300 can each keep it on UPS standby, but only through the right outlet. The resistive-only limit on the Elite 300's 4,800 W figure means its motor-start headroom should be judged against 2,400 W, not 4,800 W. That favours the F3800 Plus (6,000 W, expandable with BP3800 batteries) for wet basements where the pump cycles often. A literal 13 hp pump falls outside every candidate here.

findings.label: Outlets that give UPS backup
findings.value: Only the 3 leftmost NEMA 5-20R (120 V, 20 A) outlets
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: From the page's Q5 port-availability table: 'NEMA 5-20R (3 Leftmost Ports, UPS)'. The pump has to go in one of these three to switch over automatically.

findings.label: UPS switching time and bypass limit when charging from a 120 V wall outlet
findings.value: 20 ms; 1,440 W bypass on the UPS outlets; TT-30R marked 'No UPS'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Condition 4 (no generator, plugged into 120 V wall): 'NEMA 5-20R (3 Leftmost Ports, UPS): Output available with bypass limit of up to 1,440W'; 'TT-30R ... No UPS. Bypass limit of up to 1,440W'; 'Switching Time: 20 ms'. The tech specs also list 'AC Input Power (Bypass Mode): 1440W Max'.

findings.label: UPS outlets when a generator is connected
findings.value: Unusable (the 3 leftmost NEMA 5-20R give no output)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Conditions 2, 3, 5 and 6 (120 V or 240 V generator) mark 'NEMA 5-20R (3 Leftmost Ports, UPS)' Non-Usable. With a 120 V generator, TT-30R output works only on the L1 phase (3,000 W bypass). With a 240 V generator, L14-30R gives up to 6,000 W bypass. Generator switching: 30 ms station to generator, 50 ms generator to station.

findings.label: 240 V output limit
findings.value: No 240 V output while charging from 120 V AC
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Page text: 'The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC.' This only matters for 240 V pumps.

findings.label: Compatible expansion battery
findings.value: BP3800 (3,840 Wh, 72.8 lb), up to 6 per unit
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Page text: 'Up to 6 × Expansion Batteries (3.84kWh each)'. Base 3,840 Wh + 6 × 3,840 Wh = 26,880 Wh per unit. The page's 53.8 kWh headline appears to assume two linked units; the page doesn't explain it. No other battery model is named, and no exclusion is stated.

findings.label: Solar input with and without expansion battery
findings.value: 3,300 W single unit; 6,000 W with 1 or more expansion batteries
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Page footnote: '3,300W for single unit, 6,000W when working with 1 or more expansion batteries'.

findings.label: Bypass output limit in UPS mode
findings.note: From StorageReview's spec table. BLUETTI's product page doesn't state a bypass limit. StorageReview paraphrases the manual: UPS is 'not intended for data servers or workstations that require a high-performance UPS'.

findings.label: Loads the 4,800 W 'Power Lifting' figure covers
findings.value: Pure resistive loads only; actual output stays at 2,400 W
findings.note: StorageReview: Power Lifting 'is intended only for pure resistive loads rated between 2,400W and 4,800W' and 'the actual output power remains at 2,400W when the mode is engaged'. A sump pump motor isn't resistive, so the 4,800 W figure doesn't apply to it.

findings.label: AC outlets
findings.note: From the spec table. A standard 15 A pump plug fits the 5-20R outlets.
